subject: Urgent: SpeedBack p99 latency & throughput drop after v2.1 quant rollout
messages:
From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@speedback.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: p99 jump and throughput collapse after v2.1 quant rollout
Attachments: sample-logs.tar.gz (tar.gz, 4.2MB)

Hi Stephanie,

We rolled your new v2.1 model with q3 quant profile into production early this morning (09:30 local). Within the first 30 minutes we saw p99 latency go from ~420ms to 980ms and overall throughput fall by ~55%. Error rates for decoding (502/timeout-like failures) spiked from 0.2% to ~4.7%. This is impacting the live checkout recommendation path for ~18% of our traffic.

Our SREs captured logs and a sample latency dump (attached). We rolled the traffic split back to the v2.0 variant at 09:15 after seeing sustained degradation, but we still saw degraded tail behavior for requests routed to cached nodes — likely KV cache incompatibilities or unexpected kernel selection on the quant path.

Can you confirm if there were any changes to kernel selection heuristics or batching defaults in v2.1? We need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA for a rollback if necessary. SpeedBack is pushing this up to their CTO and CFO; they want executive-level engagement.

Priority: urgent.

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Platform, SpeedBack
liam.oconnell@speedback.com

Liam — thank you for the clear summary and for the logs. I'm really sorry you're seeing this. We're treating it as high-priority. Immediate actions we are taking now: 

- Flip traffic off v2.1 q3 everywhere (done at 08:40) and force 100% to the unquantized v2.0 variant until we verify stability.
- Infra is running a binary-level check to compare kernel selections and runtime flags between the nodes that served degraded requests and the healthy nodes — tagging as JIRA SB-1428.
- We're provisioning a short-lived burst of dedicated capacity (GPU pool) in us-west to absorb warm-up/rehydration while the cache stabilizes.
- Engineering (Irene) will capture KV cache snapshots and a decoded trace to see if the q3 path is introducing stall points.

Irene and Markus — please confirm ETA for the kernel selection diff and if we can produce a quick mitigation build that disables the new attention micro-kernel for q3. If we cannot produce a 2–4 hour mitigation, we'll need to propose a formal rollback to the customer's CTO and offer credits.

Liam — attached is a quick latency snapshot we took after flipping traffic; I'm monitoring. I'll set up a 3PM PDT bridge if needed.

Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
